analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bayern visit Hamburg days after a Champions League matchday, with Vincent Kompany's return from illness not yet confirmed and Manuel Neuer injured, so Jonas Urbig should be in goal. Hamburg have won three of four home league games and score spectacular long-range goals, but Merlin Polzin's squad is thin and Bayern have scored 29 in nine.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, 2.8 for Bayern. Bayern's scoring rate supports it and Hamburg have scored at home, but a Bayern side coming off a European midweek may rotate and manage the game. I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10 corners, six of them Bayern's. Bayern pin teams back for long spells (around 80% of the ball in Mainz), and Hamburg are likely to defend in numbers and clear wide, so I lean higher on Bayern's share.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Hamburg picked up four yellows at Frankfurt, while Bayern are rarely booked more than twice, and nothing in the news points away from an average count.

shots.text: The site has 33.5 shots. Bayern's 22.2 matches their season average, but Hamburg's 11.3 is high against a side that allowed Mainz a single shot on target, the stoppage-time goal. I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.6 on target. Bayern's accuracy, with Harry Kane also leading the league in assists, keeps their share high, and Hamburg's long-range shooters can test Urbig from distance. I stay level.
